newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sumitomo Chemical cuts domestic ethylene purchases.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo Chemical cuts domestic ethylene purchases.

text.p: Sumitomo Chemical Co Ltd said on Wednesday it has decided to cut its ethylene purchases by at least two-thirds for a three-month period from January amid high ethylene prices caused by a bullish naphtha market.
Naphtha is used as feedstock for ethylene production.
"We can't afford to continue making losses by buying expensive ethylene," a Sumitomo Chemical spokesman said.

Although Sumitomo Chemical operates its own ethylene plant, with an annual output capacity of 380,000 tonnes, it has also been purchasing 1,000 to 1,500 tonnes of ethylene a month from other domestic producers.
The petrochemical firm intends to cut purchases by at least 1,000 tonnes per month, the spokesman said.

The move will lead to a reduction in the firm's production of low-density polyethylene and styrene monomer, both of which are ethylene-derived products, by about five percent and 10 percent, respectively, he said.

Near-term naphtha prices on Asia's benchmark open-specification forward contract shot up by about 33 percent in the second half of 1996 due to tight supplies as well as high global crude prices, leaving petrochemical firms' profit margins razor thin.

Last month, Mitsubishi Chemical Corp said it would cut its ethylene production by 10 percent starting in January, and Idemitsu Petrochemical Co Ltd said it plans to cut its naphtha imports by 10 percent from January amid dwindling profit margins caused by skyrocketing naphtha prices.
